analysis.title: Travel + Leisure Co. (TNL): 3Q26 First Take: Solid quarter with 2026 guidance raised and improvement in provisions
key_insights: TNL reported 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of $283mn, in line with GS and Visible Alpha consensus of $281mn and at the high end of the $275mn-$285mn guidance range. It grew 6.4% y/y.
Gross VOI sales grew 6% y/y, in line with GSe and consensus. Tour flow growth was higher than expected and VPG growth was lower than expected.
Vacation ownership revenue was $953mn, above GSe $923mn and consensus $932mn, up 8.8% y/y. Segment adjusted EBITDA was $250mn, up 8.2% y/y, vs consensus $251mn.
Tours rose 6.5% y/y to 213k, above GSe of 210k. VPG was $3,286, down 0.5% y/y, below GSe $3,337 and consensus $3,335.
Travel & Membership revenue was $150mn, down 11.2% y/y and below GSe $155mn and consensus $159mn. Segment adjusted EBITDA was $51mn, down 12.1% y/y, vs GSe $50mn and consensus $53mn.
Adjusted diluted EPS was $2.21 vs GSe $2.09 and consensus $2.07, up 22.8% y/y.
GS says provision trends are tracking better than typical seasonal trends, down about 150bps y/y.
GS suggests the VPG shortfall may partly reflect the closing timing of Spinnaker, which added tour growth but diluted VPG.
TNL repurchased $75mn of stock (1.1mn shares), slightly below the prior quarter.

For 2026, TNL kept the VPG outlook at $3,325-$3,375 (about 2% growth at the midpoint), raised gross VOI sales to $2.625bn-$2.675bn (from $2.6bn-$2.675bn), and raised adjusted EBITDA to $1,070mn-$1,085mn (from $1,065mn-$1,085mn).
GS will look for call color on provisions for the rest of 2026 and into 2027, new owner growth, and sales force turnover.
GS keeps its Buy rating and $78 12-month price target, based on 7.0x 2027E EV/EBITDA (unchanged), vs a $65.62 price, 18.9% upside.

market_movers.rationale: Solid 3Q26 with adjusted EBITDA in line and 2026 guidance raised slightly. Provisions are improving versus normal seasonal trends. The price target is unchanged, at 7.0x 2027E EV/EBITDA.

earnings_insights: TNL 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA (per management) reported 10/27: $283mn vs GSe $281mn and consensus $281mn, up 6.4% y/y from $266mn.
TNL 3Q26 adjusted diluted EPS (per management) reported 10/27: $2.21 vs GSe $2.09 and consensus $2.07, up 22.8% y/y from $1.80.
TNL 3Q26 net revenues reported: $1,101mn vs GSe $1,077mn and consensus $1,090mn, up 5.5% y/y.
TNL 3Q26 GAAP net income reported: $108mn vs GSe $128mn and consensus $127mn. Operating income was $195mn vs GSe $236mn.
TNL 3Q26 vacation ownership revenue reported: $953mn vs GSe $923mn and consensus $932mn. Travel & Membership revenue reported: $150mn vs GSe $155mn and consensus $159mn.
TNL FY26 guidance (company outlook): VPG $3,325-$3,375 maintained vs Street $3,352. Gross VOI sales $2,625mn-$2,675mn vs Street $2,651mn. Adjusted EBITDA $1,070mn-$1,085mn vs Street $1,076mn.
GS FY26 estimates: adjusted EBITDA $1,075mn (GS est in guidance table) and EPS $7.69. FY27E EPS is $8.86 and EBITDA is $1,140mn. GS 4Q26E EPS is $2.29.
risk_factors: A weaker macro backdrop could slow consumer spending and make it harder to attract new buyers given the high upfront cost of a timeshare.
Weaker consumer confidence, rising unemployment and slower wage growth could pressure tour flow, VPG and contract sales below GS forecasts.
Higher defaults if consumer credit quality weakens could push loan loss provisions up.
